occurrences.value: THE ONE beacon-comment validator (SPEC v5 §3), shared by every mutation ingress. Rejects LF/CR/NUL, all other C0 controls, DEL, C1 controls, U+2028/U+2029, block delimiters (/* */ <!-- -->), beacon delimiters (@beacon[ / BEACON (), and Workflowy transport-entity patterns (named lt/gt/amp/quot + decimal/hex numeric refs -- fixpoint rule B). Applies the single-home leading-decoration strip so the accepted value is a fixpoint of the F12 round-trip (fixpoint rule A). Empty/whitespace normalizes to None. Commas, = and ] are SAFE and never rejected (Dan's ruling) -- internal AND trailing.

occurrences.value: The typed comment intent carried by a mutation operation (2R4E1P). preserve: no comment requested -- keep the pre-existing comment (disk-parsed authoritative, note fallback), never rejects. fill_if_empty: the DEFAULT fill semantics -- fill ONLY an empty comment; a conflicting existing comment is now KEPT with a warning (kept_existing_conflict), labels still ensured, never an error. replace: explicit opt-in overwrite. append: keep the existing comment and extend it with the requested text.

occurrences.value: THE ONE comment resolver (SPEC v5 §5 step 7 ordered contract; 2R4E1P). NORMALIZATION FIRST: requested / note_comment / disk_comment are all compared in parser-normalized form (trailing run of , and ] stripped, replicating the legacy field parser) and the value WRITTEN is the normalized form. preserve never rejects (disk value wins, note fallback, divergence is NOT an error). fill_if_empty NEVER errors: divergent note+disk -> kept_existing_conflict (disk wins); disk == requested -> idempotent; disk != requested -> kept_existing_conflict (existing comment kept, WARNING carries both texts); disk empty + note != requested -> kept_existing_conflict (the note's claim is kept); disk empty (note empty or == requested) -> fill (materialize; a re-run then noops via the idempotent rule -- invariant 10). A kept conflict means LABELS STILL ENSURED, comment kept, comment_outcome='kept_existing_conflict' + warning; re-run with replace/append to change it. replace writes the requested text (equal text -> idempotent). append keeps the existing comment and extends it: empty disk -> fill, already-appended text -> idempotent, else existing + ' ' + requested.

occurrences.value: Per-token slice-label sanitizer. THE shared plan-branch execution engine for every language helper (SPEC v5 §6). VERIFIES the plan against live disk state (dispatch path, planned operation, plan-selected physical target, raw-bytes sha256 CAS) -- a sha divergence is source_changed_since_plan, every OTHER divergence is plan_mismatch, both with ZERO write. Then executes the planned operation with the plan-resolved comment, sourcing metadata per §5 step 10: slice_labels + comment from the plan; role/kind/show_span/start/end snippets from the FRESH DISK PARSE (a labels-only mutation never rewrites them). 2R4E1P: the plan's comment decision is authoritative -- fill keeps an existing comment (a kept conflict's resolved comment IS the on-disk text; only a fill plan that would overwrite a DIFFERENT live comment is refused, existing_comment_present/plan_mismatch); replace/append overwrite/extend explicitly. Span deletes also remove the matching @beacon-close[ block. Exactly ONE atomic replacement via _write_markdown_lines_sanitized(expected_sha256=...).

occurrences.value: §4.10 (Axiom 15): the daemon's memory of the extension's archive_folder option, called from _resolve_note_session_config right after every settings reply. Raised by materialize_from_document_forest when a CANONICAL row focus ({mode:'row', uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence} that survived _canonicalize_focus) FAILS to resolve occurrence-exactly against the materialized document_forest. occurrences.value: RenderPolicy — the immutable, RENDER-FOREST-KEYED carrier of the occurrence-local render directives a focused/deprecated/chronological render needs, DECOUPLED from the tree: (1) the per-file/heading H1 rebase baseline, keyed by render-forest _index_path (covers BOTH the file-node root and the bare-MD-heading root); and (2) body suppression, carried as FOUR CAUSE-LABELED sets in DISTINCT keying disciplines — breadcrumb suppression is OCCURRENCE/index-path keyed (NOT a uuid-set, because a timestamp sort re-emits the same uuid and only SOME occurrences are focus breadcrumbs), deprecated-body suppression is uuid keyed (a per-node property), chronological-ancestor suppression (U6, ap:E03BN3) is OCCURRENCE/index-path keyed like breadcrumb (every non-leaf of the final render forest on a chronological render — computed ONLY inside the materializer from the producer-supplied chronological boolean), and lens-scaffold-ancestor suppression ([ap:I506WY], unit 5g) is OCCURRENCE/index-path keyed too (on a LENS render the connective scaffolding above the lens's input roots renders heading-only even in document order; computed ONLY inside the materializer from the producer-supplied lens_scaffold_ids the shared lens projection derives). The cause label is load-bearing: emit_body_false_for(render_key, uuid) lets BOTH renderers consume the THREE occurrence-keyed causes (breadcrumb ∪ chronological-ancestor ∪ lens-scaffold-ancestor) via the render_key branch, while deprecated-body suppression stays Markdown-only (include_deprecated). occurrences.value: THE normalized cache-render request object -- the keystone of the cache-render pipeline. ONE immutable, frozen dataclass every cache-projected render (raw root dump / slice / slice+override / Lightning Rod) normalizes to before projection+render, so the same shared render pipeline is driven identically from EITHER origin: the SERVER (glimpse / lightning_rod MCP tools, and the push twin _glimpse_push_slice_to_modal) OR the CLIENT (Apply button, Refresh, row click, Lightning Rod ribbon). The origin fills the object with what it already knows and passes it through -- the server NEVER queries the client for a value it can supply itself (a server push forwards headings_only explicitly rather than inheriting the client dock toggle). Field groups: SOURCE/SCOPE identity (kind + root_uuid + group_id/group_name + opaque lightning selection); SELECTION/TRAVERSAL knobs (match_scope = WHERE to look for a tag/text match; descend_policy = HOW FAR to walk, a Phase-1 traversal boundary; exclude_completed); VIEW knobs (sort_by [wire spelling 'none'|'created'|'modified'] / sort_direction / since / recent_by ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a): the recency basis of a 'newest' item_count selection; None = resolve at apply) / headings_only / ancestor_notes [U6 teaching opt-out of the chronological ancestor-note suppression, default false]); OUTPUT/RENDER contract (as_markdown / content_format / tree_mode). Two orthogonal axes kept strictly separate and NEVER conflated: match_scope (selection predicate) vs descend_policy+exclude_completed (traversal) -- and descend_policy lives at the TOP LEVEL, never inside a Lightning Rod selection (which is about WHAT matches, not how far to walk) and never in Phase 2/3/4 (presentation policy). WIRE CONTRACT: the nested render_spec blob is the SOLE scope/view contract on every render_slice_modal / render_slice_row / apply_slice_in_dock frame -- the only flat frame keys are the transport envelope (action / request_id / endpoint_id / row / max_prerender_chars). occurrences.value: SHARED UUID-prefix fallback resolver (tool-neutral). occurrences.value: LAYER-1 UUID PRIMITIVE -- the single confluence point for ALL UUID-like node-handle resolution. Folds the EXACT-hit check and the shared prefix kernel (_resolve_uuid_with_prefix_fallback) into ONE pure function used by beacon_get_code_snippet / workflowy_scry / add_to_anchor / update_note_session / root_uuid GLIMPSE / the tag path. HYBRID CACHE LOAD (Commit 1.5, per Opus+GPT-5.5+Dan): nodes_by_id is OPTIONAL. If a caller already holds the cache map (because it needs it AFTER resolution -- ancestor walk, node classification, subtree projection), it PASSES the map and there is NO double read. If a caller only needs resolution (the tag path), it passes client= and nodes_by_id=None, and the primitive self-loads via the shared load_nodes_by_id_from_cache helper. EITHER WAY the primitive RETURNS the nodes_by_id it used, so a self-loading caller can reuse the exact same map downstream. Exactly one of {nodes_by_id, client} must be provided. Still does NOT render error strings (callers keep their own miss-policy: beacon SURFACES ambiguity as a loud did-you-mean carrying the candidates [ap:G5C9BX]; anchors SURFACE _anchor_uuid_cache_miss_error; scry SURFACES on ambiguous, FALLS THROUGH on no-match). Tri-state return + nodes_by_id: {success:True, resolved_uuid, input_kind:'exact_uuid'|'uuid_prefix', nodes_by_id} on hit; {success:False, candidates, matched_prefix_len, truncated, input_kind:None, nodes_by_id} on ambiguous; {success:False, input_kind:None, nodes_by_id} on unresolved. key_prefix passes to the kernel (slice-group 'grp-' parity); the slice-group resolver stays OUT of this wrapper by design (matches the config map, not the nodes cache). BRACKETED-UUID LENIENCY (Dan, 2026): the candidate passes through unwrap_bracketed_uuid_handle FIRST -- an AP-ID-style bracket wrapper around a pure-hex >=8-char body ('[a2e552e3]' / '[full-uuid]') is stripped ONCE here so EVERY funnel surface inherits the leniency with no per-site branching; '[ap:CORE]' and bracketed non-hex cores are never unwrapped and stay AP-leg territory. HANDLE-CORRECTION ECHO (23db916f): on a kernel UNIQUE hit the wrapper compares the kernel's matched_prefix_len against the normalized (key-prefix-stripped, hyphen-stripped, bracket-unwrapped) supplied length and records ONE correction via handle_corrections.record_handle_correction IFF the handle was SHAVED (matched_prefix_len < supplied length) -- an exact hit, an AP-ID and a clean prefix that matched at its own full length stay silent; _mcp_operation_result_finalizer drains the record into the one 'resolved: <short> <name> (corrected from <supplied>)' echo line / resolved_corrections key. The return SHAPE is unchanged (still pure tri-state + nodes_by_id); the echo state is side-band. ARCHIVE READS TWO-PHASE (universe param, U1; rev 2 ruling [ap:WNV4ZW]): live first -- the EXACT hit runs over the LIVE partition only and the kernel over the LIVE partition -- and the archive phase (the kernel over the ARCHIVE partition, or the fallback gate when the map carries no partition) runs only after a TOTAL live miss; universe='live'/'archive' restrict to one phase, and an archive record's key is never a live exact hit. The EXACT archived full UUID beats a SHAVED live match in EVERY mode (E2/Axiom 2; the side-effect-free is_exact_archived_id is asked at the shave, the beacon family excepted — Axiom 12), so a read serves the archive and a write stays unresolved for its site's archive-aware refusal; the re-run request stays the gate's job, in the archive phase only. Callers tell an archive answer by is_archive_record(nodes_by_id[resolved]) -- the return shape is unchanged.

Rules: supplied trailing #tags -> ProtectedNameViolation(tags_in_name_rejected), even when identical to current; a supplied leading [ap:] absent-from or different-than current -> ProtectedNameViolation(ap_id_mutation_rejected); an IDENTICAL existing AP-ID may be repeated and is emitted exactly once in stored spelling; omitted AP-ID/tags auto-preserve. LEADING EMOJI RUN (Z8Q0PF+LITF2F): a free-form rename also preserves the ordinary title's existing leading emoji run -- you need not pass an emoji -- unless the supplied title begins with its own run (explicit wins); replace_leading_emoji=True hands the run to the supplied title wholesale (its run replaces the existing one, its absence clears it; the byte-verbatim fast path does not bypass the preservation). Validation order is deterministic: tags first, then AP-ID. Narrow internal channels only (never a generic bypass): tag_transform rewrites Dock locality; assign_ap_core adds a reserved AP core; remove_ap_id removes only the leading AP token; leading_emoji_mutation carries the typed replace/prepend/append request of the node emoji verbs (update_emoji / prepend_emoji / append_emoji) against only the leading emoji run of the ordinary name section after any AP. A mid-title [ap:X] or middle/right emoji is ordinary title content. Pure; no I/O.

occurrences.value: Build the actionable cache-miss error message for an anchor UUID that did not resolve exactly. Leads with the hallucination/mistype hypothesis (the dominant real cause -- agents fabricate the UUID tail from the first segment) rather than the old 'refresh the cache' staleness framing. When prefix-fallback candidates exist (the supplied UUID's prefix matched MULTIPLE nodes) it appends a 'did you mean?' list of full real UUIDs + node names so the agent self-corrects in one step instead of refreshing-and-retrying the same bad UUID. When there are no candidates it falls back to suggesting a cache refresh (genuine staleness / wrong vault).

occurrences.value: note_file ingestion for add_to_anchor: read a UTF-8 text file through the ONE host-aware path resolver (tool_path_resolution: translated where a mapping exists, refused loudly where none does) and normalize it into the standard single-node ETCH payload [{name: file STEM (extension deliberately dropped so the node is never mistaken for a Cartographer-mapped file), note: raw text}] -- the guarded capture funnel downstream (resolver -> guard -> parse-peek -> etch -> tags) then runs byte-for-byte unchanged. LOUD failures (NetworkError): empty/relative path, missing file, directory, non-UTF-8 (never errors='replace' -- the note is ingested verbatim). Newlines normalized CRLF/CR -> LF via universal-newlines read (the system's pure-LF note convention). A Workflowy trailing-#tag region in the STEM is REJECTED via the canonical split_name_and_tags (note_file tags MUST go through tags=, never the filename -- enforced, not advisory). AP-ID FILENAME CONVENTION (Dan, 2026): a leading '[ap_CORE]' handle in the stem -- the colon of '[ap:CORE]' is illegal in Windows filenames -- is canonicalized to '[ap:CORE]' (lowercase ap + uppercased core, matching _AP_ID_LEADING_RE so the handle resolves); echoed via meta['ap_id_transformed']. OPTIONAL name_override (Dan, 2026): when supplied, the override (stripped, non-empty) is used as the node name VERBATIM, and the stem-derived behaviors that exist ONLY to produce a name (tag-region rejection + AP-ID transform) are SKIPPED -- the name comes from the caller, not the filename. meta gains name_override=True (False when absent).

occurrences.value: ƒ _merge_file_note_header(old_note: str, fresh_line_count: int, pending_path_segment: str | None = None)

THE ONE preservation-safe FILE-header merge (FILE-NOTE HEADER FRESHNESS, Dan 2026): merges a fresh LINE COUNT into an existing FILE note's OWNED header region — the strict line-0 Path: line plus the immediately following contiguous LINE COUNT:/Source-SHA1: metadata lines — and preserves every other byte of the note (suffix, spacing, terminal newline) verbatim. Drops legacy Source-SHA1: lines (no operational reader; deliberately hash-free), applies an optional deferred portability Path-segment migration inside the same preserved note, refuses non-Path-first notes (Root:/MD_PATH dummy/ordinary) by returning None rather than inserting a header. Pure; no I/O; callers raise loudly on None.

occurrences.value: _render_anchor_tree_raw_text(anchor_tree, global_count, local_count, show_local, compact, max_chars, max_description_chars, show_description, favorites_only, favorites_fallback, favorite_count, total_dock_count, favorite_tag_hint)

Pure anchor-inventory raw-text serializer: renders the anchor-only tree as a UUID-left / indented-name-right text outline. Domain serializer like Lightning Rod gather, deliberately NOT a Markdown/node-tree render or Stage-1/Stage-2 path. TWO modes: legacy (the defaults -- byte-for-byte the established widget clipboard format: full 36-char UUID column, blank line per row, '  [local]' suffix) and compact=True (the consolidated anchor.dock.list default: an 8-char resolver-compatible [prefix] column that NEVER indents -- only the Dock name receives two spaces per Dock-ancestry level -- plus ' ⭐' favorite (BEFORE ' Ⓛ') and ' Ⓛ' local markers, no blank spacer rows, and a one-line teaching header ending detail='full' for JSON). The favorites kwargs (favorites_only EFFECTIVE value, favorites_fallback, favorite_count, total_dock_count, favorite_tag_hint) drive the compact header grammar ONLY -- fallback header says 'no favorites configured: showing all' + the composed #base--word hint; an effective favorites header reports shown/favorites/hidden counts with the 'favorites_only=false to show' teaching. [ap:YLHDIN] part 2: compact rows carry the Dock's FIRST description line as a ' -- excerpt' tail after the markers (_compact_description_excerpt: the first non-empty line of the row's metadata-stripped description, middle-ellipsised; show_description=true default, max_description_chars default 120, 0 hides; a row without a description gets no tail at all). Legacy mode IGNORES the favorites AND description kwargs (byte-identical).

occurrences.value: ⚡ add_to_anchor(self, parent_uuid: str, nodes, tags, note_file, content, name)

Guarded capture wrapper around workflowy_etch: etch one or many nodes under an anchor (parent_uuid) AFTER the shared placement guard (_anchor_target_guard_error) confirms the target is not a FOLDER and not a NON-Markdown mapped file. Fails CLOSED on an uncached parent. Surfaces a mapped_subtree F12+3 advisory when the parent is a Markdown file / inside Markdown. This is the ONLY value-add over calling workflowy_etch directly (the guard); dialect-neutral by design (the anchor's dialect -- todo/note/brainstorm/etc -- is unknown at call time). THREE payload forms, EXACTLY ONE required (loud on both/neither -- deliberately unlike workflowy_etch's nodes_file, which silently WINS over inline nodes): `nodes` (an ETCH forest) XOR `note_file` (an absolute-path UTF-8 text file -> exactly ONE node: file STEM = NAME, raw text = NOTE, normalized at the edge via _node_payload_from_note_file so the funnel is untouched; filename-embedded #tags REJECTED -- tags must go through tags=; a leading '[ap_CORE]' filename handle is canonicalized to '[ap:CORE]') XOR `content` (a raw string -- write_file-parity -- with REQUIRED `name`; normalized at the edge via _node_payload_from_content into ONE node: name = NAME verbatim, content = NOTE verbatim; a trailing #tag in name is ALLOWED since it is directly authored). OPTIONAL `name` with note_file: overrides the stem as the node name (stem-derived tag-region check + AP-ID transform SKIPPED).

SCRY includes the requested root and its note. Size truncation explicitly reserves the root before retaining descendants (flat export order is not traversal order); file output delegates to the existing bulk exporter, which retains the root note alongside root identity. No second root fetch or cache path. Chain-1 W4 (F5): in a SINK operation (output_file) whose root names a visible archived node, the total-miss fall-through RAISES the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal before the exporter — never the historical zero-node file-mode success with no file; non-sink reads keep today's flow (the fallback re-run serves archived roots).

occurrences.value: LAYER-4 snippet EXTRACTION -- the back half split out of beacon_get_code_snippet (Commit 2). THE completed filter for dock.peek lives HERE and nowhere else: rows already flagged completed are excluded from the candidate pool by default on EVERY path -- recency views (recent=N or a timestamp sort_by) AND the plain document-order inventory -- unless include_completed=true opts back in (U6/J11: the inventory no longer lists ✓ rows by default). occurrences.value: THE generic Stage-1 SELECTION primitive: walk the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, admit a node iff member_predicate(node) is True, and build the minimal connective subtree (every admitted node + all ancestors up to and including root_uuid, children priority-ordered). Returns a nested {id,name,note,children} root, or None if root_uuid is absent from the cache. Every cache-sourced selection source converges here by supplying its own admit predicate over ONE tree-walk machinery: slice groups (the is_slice_member closure, via the build_slice_subtree_from_cache wrapper), the raw-dump root GLIMPSE (member_all -> lambda node: True), and Lightning Rod tag/text-search predicates. Two orthogonal TRAVERSAL policies ride alongside the membership predicate: exclude_completed prunes a completed CHILD at admit time (its whole subtree becomes invisible; no downstream --expand can un-hide it), and boundary_predicate is a stop-recursion boundary (a child satisfying it is still visited/admitted and anchors the connective spine, but the walk does not descend into it -- it renders as a leaf). Both policies exempt the root by construction (each is tested only when deciding whether to descend into a CHILD). A THIRD traversal policy, max_depth (ap:EPR86W part a; the spec's recursive=false maps to 1): the walk descends only while the CURRENT node's depth < max_depth (root = depth 0), so max_depth=1 renders the root + its DIRECT children and nothing deeper -- child Docks and plain nodes alike; descend_policy is moot under the cap (the cap stops the descent first). The same gate stops the materialize recursion, so a capped node is childless in the output by construction. None (the default) is the ordinary unbounded walk -- byte-for-byte prior behavior; only the raw-root surfaces thread the cap (a membership selection is unbounded by construction and refuses recursive=false loudly at the spec normalizer).

occurrences.value: LIGHTNING ROD gather-tags: union of all REAL '#'-stripped tags found under root_uuid in the /nodes-export cache, sorted + de-duped. match_scope (SELECTION-stage scope knob) picks WHERE tags are harvested: 'name_and_note' (default) -> name AND note (strict recognizer); 'name' -> the NAME's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter (_core_trailing_name_tags; a mid-title prose '#tag' or a note-only '#tag' is not gathered) -- matched to the two render modes so a gather->render_tags handoff surveys exactly the fields the render will filter on. boundary_predicate (Phase-C descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors', default None) is a STOP-RECURSION traversal knob: when a descendant satisfies it (a child anchor), that node's OWN tags are still harvested (visible signpost) but its subtree is NOT surveyed -- so gather and a subsequent render_tags see the SAME bounded universe (root exempt). Uses the STRICT extract_strict_tags_from_text recognizer (NOT the generalized Workflowy-search harvester) so it does NOT return junk harvested from '#' glued inside prose/code (').strip()', 'f8-expand),', etc.). Lightning Rod is unmoored/divergent-from-Workflowy, so gather is free to be smarter about what counts as a genuine tag. Pure, no rendering, no pipeline -- the discovery call whose result feeds a follow-up Lightning Rod render_tags.

occurrences.value: LIGHTNING ROD gather SERIALIZER -- the tag-domain peer of the node-tree composer. Turns a flat, sorted tag list (from gather_tags_in_subtree) into a prefix-grouped, hyphen-segment-nested RAW TEXT outline (4 spaces per level, alphabetical within a level). This is the intentional serialization seam for gather: gather produces a TAG SET (not a node tree), so its correct serializer is THIS pure function, NOT the node-tree render tail render_stage2_filter_sort (which would need a fake tree). The shared universal contract is 'one final rendered string', re-unified at the delivery boundary, not at the tree renderer. HYPHEN RULE (Dan): a run of >=1 hyphens collapses to a SINGLE separator, then split -- so double-hyphen postfixes (--deprecated/--suppress/--expand) are NOT special-cased and just become an ordinary trailing segment. SYNTHESIZED PARENTS: an intermediate segment path that is not itself a literal gathered tag still gets an outline header line for readability; those synthetic headers appear ONLY in this text, never in the caller's literal `tags` array. Pure / no I/O -- the tag-set analog of _build_markdown_preview_from_tree.

occurrences.value: PHASE 2 (the heart) — given a VALID Phase-1 subtree + active slice config, compute the expansion plan {collapse_suppressed, collapse_deprecated, expand}. Annotates each node, applies the "don't collapse a deprecated node through a live in-slice descendant" rescue rule, normalizes each set topmost-only, and resolves cross-set conflicts via the ASYMMETRIC merge: a contraction dominates a nested expansion, but an expansion does NOT dominate a nested contraction -- so a suppress/deprecated pocket can survive inside an --expand region. BOTH Phase 3 (server) and the JS client executeF8ExpansionPlan execute the plan EXPAND FIRST, THEN collapse_suppressed, THEN collapse_deprecated -- expanding first so a nested contraction is not overwritten by a later re-hydration. Also emits the Tier-2 pending_* live-GUI-sync metadata + the deprecated-body-suppression body_suppressed_ids set (surviving --deprecated nodes render header-only). match_scope (default name_and_note) threads the SELECTION-stage scope into THREE questions: the rescue's liveness membership (compute_live's is_slice_member; post-Sol-audit Finding 2), the promotion pass's ACTIVE-self check (node_is_live_self title-harvests under 'name'), AND -- 084 ruling -- the --expand/--suppress/--deprecated OPERATION classification itself (annotate passes it into classify_node_tags: under 'name' a family postfix counts only in the name's TRAILING tag region; under 'name_and_note' it also counts in the note). The global-never tag is TRAILING-only under every scope (name_has_global_never_tag).

occurrences.value: PHASE 3 (no-DOM path) -- apply a Phase-2 expansion plan to the Phase-1 membership subtree IN MEMORY, emulating the browser's executeF8ExpansionPlan against the live DOM. Mandated order EXPAND FIRST, THEN COLLAPSE: (1) expand, (2) collapse_suppressed, (3) collapse_deprecated -- expanding first so a contraction nested inside an expanded region survives (collapse-first would let the expansion re-hydrate and overwrite the nested collapse). occurrences.value: Pure recursive LensSpec evaluator. A group/tags atom that OMITS its own match_scope takes ctx.default_match_scope (the surface threads 'name' for a recipe render, 'name' for sift tag atoms); an explicit per-atom match_scope always wins. Chain-1 r2 (F5): a sink (write/export/purge_preview) whose GROUP atom's STORED root names a visible archived node raises ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError with the universal §5.3.2 envelope — the same answer _resolve_root gives an override root — while every other resolution failure stays a path-bearing LensSpecError. Chain-2 r1 (F1): a group atom's INHERITED stored root resolves through the SAME _resolve_root/Stage-0 resolve_root seam an override root uses (the shared two-phase composite resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle), so an exported-and-deleted stored root is served by the automatic fallback re-run and an include-mode run records the archive answer (banner + provenance); a live stored root resolves to itself, and every resolution failure falls through to the pre-existing refusal check + group_resolution_failed error unchanged. Chain-2 r2 (R1): the inherited branch resolves under the STORED-IDENTITY policy — a SHAVED corrective match is REJECTED (never adopted as the atom's scope, even with no archive folder), the speculative correction echo is surgically discarded, and the rejection falls into the same miss path (group_resolution_failed / the archived-stored-root sink refusal); explicit override atoms keep today's forgiving correction, echo included, and an exact archived record still beats a shave upstream (E2).

occurrences.value: Local MCP-server request_id demultiplexer for the single server<->broker WebSocket. The BROKER already routes correlated replies to the correct MCP server process; this object performs the SECOND demux layer INSIDE that process: _ws_request_response registers request_id->Future before sending, and websocket_handler.put(...) resolves the exact Future instead of dropping frames through a shared FIFO. Non-correlated / unmatched frames still fall through to the legacy queue for existing consumers. This is what makes nested/concurrent Direction-A calls safe (server->tab command triggers tab->server handler triggers server->tab config read, etc.) without waiters cannibalizing each other's replies.

Thin wrapper: the canonical implementation now lives in api_client_nexus (single source of truth, co-located with _extract_path_header_from_note + _classify_node_map_state); imported here via a function-scoped local import to avoid the api_client_nexus->server cycle, mirroring the other unguarded server->client local imports. occurrences.value: _compose_render_scope(kind, group_id, group_name, root_uuid, sort_by, sort_direction, since, headings_only)

Build the SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE render_scope echo object for a cache-projected render. This is the ONE object every consumer (client adoptRenderScope -> per-tab render state + ribbon widgets + footer; and the MCP push tool output) treats as the normalized ground truth of what was ACTUALLY rendered, regardless of which SURFACE (ribbon click or MCP glimpse() call) triggered the render. Carries ONLY the normalized structured render-defining fields: scope identity (kind/group_id/group_name/root_uuid) + view params (sort_by/sort_direction/since object-or-null/headings_only). There is no pre-composed display string -- the status footer is the ONE consumer that renders a human string, composing it from THESE fields, so string-composition lives in exactly one place. kind is 'slice' (group at its own root), 'slice_override' (group tags scoped to an override root), 'raw_root' (bare root_uuid raw dump, no group -> the footer labels it 'raw dump of <root8>'), or 'lightning_rod' (a temporary Lightning Rod selection via the `lightning` param, which takes PRECEDENCE). LIGHTNING SELECTION: a lightning render carries ONE opaque `selection` object {mode:'gather'|'render_tags'|'render_search'|'render_symbols', + per-mode fields (tags+postfix_policy | query/query_mode | symbols/root_uuids/favor) + match_scope} that the client round-trips VERBATIM for BEHAVIOR (routing is by selection.mode, never selection_kind). selection_kind ('gather'|'tags'|'search'|'symbols') + workflowy_search_equivalent are DERIVED from selection.mode and are DISPLAY-ONLY (footer/status-bar label). UNMOORED SIGNAL: live_gui_sync_supported is a TOP-LEVEL bool emitted for EVERY kind (+ live_gui_sync_skipped_reason naming why when False) -- False for a raw dump (no membership search), a descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' render (inexpressible as a Workflowy search), a search_too_many_variants refusal, or any lightning selection; the client surfaces the unmoored state on the yellow bar. It is DISPLAY/observability only, never a behavior driver. EVERY kind also carries the explicit CONTENT/TREE CONTRACT fields content_format ('markdown'|'raw_text') + tree_mode ('render_tree'|'root_only') so the client never guesses how to paint the one rendered string or populate the top-half list (only a lightning GATHER is raw_text/root_only today). Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

occurrences.value: Phase-E1 SPEC-AWARE BRIDGE to the ONE render_scope composer. Given a RESOLVED RenderProjectionSpec (kind/root/group already canonicalized by the caller's resolution step -- NOT the raw incoming spec), DELEGATE to _compose_render_scope by unpacking exactly the scalar params it already takes (Option A, Dan-decided: delegate, do NOT reimplement from spec.to_render_scope_fields(), so there stays ONE render_scope-assembly implementation and this never becomes a second scope factory / caller-side fabrication site). The is_raw_dump / root_overridden booleans the scalar composer wants are read straight off the spec's kind-derived properties (spec.is_raw_dump / spec.root_overridden), and sort_by is passed via spec.sort_by_internal() (the ONE wire-'none'<->internal-None translation). search_too_many_variants is a POST-RENDER fact (not a spec input field, per invariant 5) so it is threaded as an explicit kwarg here, exactly as the scalar composer already accepts it. This is the E1 seam that lets every downstream server call site (modal handler E3, content-return GLIMPSE paths E4, push frame E5) compose render_scope FROM the same spec it projected from, instead of from a parallel bag of locals -- the two-parallel-assembly-points seam Phase E removes. Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

Mirrors _resolve_tag_node_id but for mutators: routes the supplied handle through the Layer-3 universal resolver client.resolve_node_handle(prefer='uuid', allow_uuid=True, allow_symbol=True) so a mutator gains the SAME UUID-hallucination grace the tag tools got in Commit 1 (exact hit -> unique prefix -> ambiguous STOP -> symbol fallback) instead of posting a raw node_id to a zero-tolerance REST endpoint. UUID leg self-loads the cache (resolve-only; no map reuse downstream). DIFFERENCE from the tag path: a mutator that cannot identify its target must FAIL LOUDLY, not silently no-op -- so on ambiguous/unresolved this RAISES RuntimeError with actionable guidance (candidates listed on ambiguity) rather than returning a friendly no-op dict. On success returns the single resolved UUID. label is the tool name, used only in messages. occurrences.value: GLIMPSE `since` Form-A window PARSER. Parses a time-window token into a duration in SECONDS (timestamps are epoch-seconds). Accepts a unit-suffixed integer/float -- s(econds) m(inutes) h(ours) d(ays) w(eeks) -- e.g. '3d','1w','12h','90m','45s'; a BARE number is interpreted as DAYS ('7' == '7d'), the common case. Whitespace-tolerant, case-insensitive. Returns None for a blank/None/garbage/non-positive token so the caller can raise an actionable error. Pure. | GLIMPSE `since` PRUNE -- the shared leaf-branch filter run LAST (after Phase1/2/3 AND after the timestamp reorder), on the already-final sorted forest. Decomposes the forest into root->leaf branches (same DFS the sort uses), keeps a branch iff its branch-date (via the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static -- created=leaf createdAt, modified=branch-max modifiedAt, IDENTICAL to the sort) is beyond the pivot: ascending -> STRICTLY GREATER than pivot (most-recent tail; the pivot node itself excluded, everything newer kept); descending -> STRICTLY LESS than pivot (the commensurate 'oldest tail', a don't-care corner but done right). A branch with no resolvable date is DROPPED (can't prove it's in the window). Then trie-merges the surviving branches back into a tree via the SAME _reorder pass with sort_by carried through, so straddled ancestors re-emit exactly as in the unfiltered render. Returns a NEW forest (inputs untouched); empty list when nothing survives.

occurrences.value: GLIMPSE `since` Form-A (time-window) PIVOT. Data-relative leading edge (Dan): the pivot is the branch-date of the MOST RECENT leaf branch in the ALREADY-FINAL forest (ascending) minus the window -- so 'last 1 week' on data whose newest branch is 2 years old means the week ENDING at that 2-year-old edge, NOT wall-clock now. Descending flips to the OLDEST edge plus the window (the don't-care commensurate corner). Uses the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static for every branch date so it matches the sort. Returns the pivot epoch-seconds, or None if no branch has a resolvable date (caller then returns the tree unfiltered rather than erroring on empty data).

occurrences.value: GLIMPSE `since="curated"` FORM-B PIVOT (the self-maintaining curation cursor). Walks the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, finds every node that has been CURATED = carries any tag matching an active slice prefix INCLUDING --deprecated variants but EXCLUDING the --suppress/--expand PRESENTATION variants (via node_is_curated_for_prefixes, threaded with the render caller's resolved match_scope -- the SAME SELECTION-stage scope knob Stage-1 membership uses, 'name' = title only so a note-body family tag never moves the cursor, 'name_and_note' = default NAME+NOTE -- deliberately looser than slice MEMBERSHIP on the triage axis, because deprecating a tag is itself a curation act the user must not re-encounter; suppressing/expanding one is a lens carve-out, NOT triage, and must not move the cursor -- Session-019 curated-cursor fix + match_scope plumbing). For each curated node it computes that node's branch-date using the SAME rule the sort uses (_branch_timestamp_key_static over the node's root->leaf cache path: created=the curated node's own createdAt; modified=branch-max modifiedAt down to it), and returns the MAX (ascending; MIN for descending) = the high-water mark. Everything strictly newer than this in the shared-tail prune is the UNCURATED tail. Returns None when NOTHING under root is curated yet (no group tag anywhere) so the tail shows the whole subtree (all of it is 'new since last curated'). Cache-only; pure aside from the cache read.

occurrences.value: render_stage2_filter_sort(spec, final_subtree, cache_by_id, output_file, source_meta, since_pivot_ts, since_form, body_suppressed_ids, max_nodes, member_predicate)

STAGE 2 (filter+sort+render): the shared render/sort/write tail for every cache-sourced GLIMPSE (slice-group, bare root_uuid, and Lightning Rod). Runs OVER an already-built STAGE-1 base tree and does PRESENTATION only -- it never re-decides membership. Delegates the sort/since/empty-window/count prep to prepare_stage2_render_forest, then renders through the same composer the live-DOM GLIMPSE uses (_build_markdown_preview_from_tree in markdown mode, _annotate_preview_ids_and_build_tree in full/UUID mode), optionally resolving a row focus to render one node's option-Y view. headings_only renders also carry dock.peek's four-field end-of-line vocabulary ([ap:UH0UOU]): the source_metrics index is built once here (build_render_source_metrics over this render's top-level root) and rides the policy; managed source lines (Cartographer/beacon markers) stay bare. Optionally writes a single compact .md (full-mode disk export is caller-guarded, not here). Merges the caller's source_meta into the payload. NODE LIMIT ([ap:O3MDOY] half 2): the optional max_nodes/member_predicate pair -- passed ONLY by the search surfaces (slice_group.sift / lightning_rod.render_search headings tiers) -- caps the final forest to the first N MATCHING nodes AFTER the sort and the since prune via cap_forest_to_first_node_count, recomputes node_count/depth over what actually renders, and echoes node_limit_applied (the shaper's node-limit line composes from it); every other caller passes neither and stays byte-identical. LENS SCAFFOLD ([ap:I506WY], unit 5g): the optional lens_scaffold_ids set -- passed ONLY by the lens render tails (the caller folds the ancestor_notes opt-out) -- forwards the lens's connective scaffolding above the input roots to BOTH materialize calls' lens-scaffold-ancestor cause, so that ancestor path renders headings-only in Markdown AND full/UUID mode, document order included; every other caller passes nothing and stays byte-identical. Knows NOTHING about slice-group or root_uuid resolution. REPOSITORY VIEW (U1): with spec.repository_view the projection (_repository_view_forest) runs after the prepare/cap steps (a multi-root render refuses), the projected forest materializes with document order / no focus / no chronological suppression, D = composed + one final newline, the payload and the output_file ack carry the repository_view counts (+ document on the in-memory payload), and the file write delivers D exactly -- never the coherence advisory (§6.3).

occurrences.value: async _resolve_lightning_rod_symbol_items_from_cache(cache_by_id, symbols, resolved_roots, suppress_tags, favor, allow_anchor_points)

Shared per-input symbol resolution core for Lightning Rod. Resolves every requested UUID/symbol exactly once, preserves the original input item beside its resolved UUID, applies root scoping and optional suppression filtering, and returns ordered per-item records plus the classic render_symbols buckets. AP-ID ITEMS (ap:APSYMB): an '[ap:CORE]' / 'ap:CORE' item (any case; a BARE core is NOT accepted -- grammar guard _RENDER_SYMBOLS_AP_ID_ITEM_RE) resolves via the shared resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle BEFORE the UUID-shaped / symbol classification -- but ONLY when allow_anchor_points=True, which is passed ONLY by the render wrapper (_project_render_symbols_from_cache); the beacon-mutation modes call with the default False and are categorically unaffected (anchor points are ephemeral-read-only). Used by render_symbols and the beacon-mutation modes so mutation never re-resolves UUIDs or guesses which operation belongs to which resolved node. BRACKETED-UUID ITEMS (Dan, 2026): an item whose AP-ID-style brackets wrap a pure-hex >=8-char body ('[a2e552e3]' / '[full-uuid]') is unwrapped via the SAME pure normalizer the Layer-1 primitive consumes (unwrap_bracketed_uuid_handle) BEFORE the _uuid_shaped routing classification, so it ROUTES to the UUID leg instead of falling to the symbol leg; '[ap:CORE]' items (colon => non-hex) and bracketed non-hex cores ('[K7M2QF]') are never unwrapped and route exactly as before.

occurrences.value: Shared Q3 beacon batch orchestrator for ensure/remove. Ordinary per-item resolution and returned preflight failures are ledger rows, not batch vetoes; valid items continue through the existing JIT/CAS writer. Scope/cache/infrastructure failures and duplicate/disk-target collisions still abort. The ONE all-target lease acquisition, ownership, cancellation, and cleanup paths are unchanged; any lease refusal still blocks all eligible writes. Disk-only with complete partial-success ledger. Policy addendum: docs/BEACON-BATCH-PARTIAL-SUCCESS.md. NON-BLOCKING (NBBW): Phase B resolution runs in a worker thread (private loop, cache-only) and the client preflight/plan/commit bodies run in worker threads -- the commit thread is never abandoned on cancellation, so the lease release in finally still follows the last disk write. GLOBAL SUPPRESSION: symbol resolution honours #wfy-suppress via _beacon_symbol_suppress_tags (fail-loud read); a suppressed-only item is an item-local all_suppressed row, never written. COMMENT CONFLICTS (2R4E1P): a fill-mode conflict is KEPT, never an error -- the labels are still ensured, comment_outcome='kept_existing_conflict' rides every row status (committed/noop alike) with a warning carrying BOTH texts; the batch result gains a top-level warnings list and a summary.comment_conflicts_kept count, which make_mutation_ack lifts to the ack's warnings. ATOMIC OPT-IN ([ap:LPC157] residue): spec.atomic=true (default false) restores the strict preflight veto AFTER Phase C and BEFORE lease acquisition -- any item failure leaves every other row not_run with zero writes and no lease (the failing item keeps its error row); a mid-batch commit failure is still per item (writes are individually CAS-atomic, no rollback exists). ONE-LINE SUMMARY: the result carries a top-level summary_line ('N committed · M noop · K failed (...)' -- the single failure's symbol/kind/reason, else the distinct failure kinds) so an agent can act without reading the ledger.

occurrences.value: async _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache(slice_group, as_markdown, output_file, sort_by, sort_direction, target_tab)

Cache-only GLIMPSE path for a slice group (no DOM/extract_dom): the content-return originator of a slice render. Reads the live slice-group config (tab-agnostic get_slice_group_config -- the ONLY WS touch, for OPTIONS not DOM), resolves the requested slice_group id-OR-name via the SHARED _resolve_slice_group_handle (exact id -> unique 'grp-' prefix -> case-insensitive name fallback -- the SAME resolver the push path uses, so the two can't drift), derives its root_uuid + active prefixes + effective sort, optionally resolves a root_uuid_override (the slice_override scope) or a stop-at-child-anchors boundary predicate, and builds ONE RenderProjectionSpec BEFORE projecting so STAGE-1 admission (exclude_completed/match_scope) is read off the spec. Runs STAGE 1 via the shared funnel build_stage1_base_tree (Phase 1 membership -> Phase 2 plan -> Phase 3 collapse/expand -> Phase 4 zombie prune), computes the curated pivot when since='curated', then hands the base tree + the SAME spec to the shared STAGE-2 tail render_stage2_filter_sort. active_prefixes / postfix words / global_never / cache_by_id are live-config OPERANDS, deliberately NOT spec fields. Output is structurally identical to a live-DOM GLIMPSE of the same expanded slice, so a session can be initialized with no human at the Workflowy GUI. Chain-1 r2 (F5): a sink aimed at a stored root that names a visible archived node raises the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal before any render/file work. Chain-2 r1 (F1): with NO override, the EFFECTIVE STORED root itself resolves through the SAME shared composite resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle the override root gets (live legs first, then the archive legs — the fallback gate and record_archive_served ride inside it), so an exported-and-deleted stored root is served by the automatic fallback re-run (banner + provenance via the finalizer) and an include-mode run records the archive answer; a live stored root resolves to itself unchanged, and an unknown one stays unresolved for the Stage-1 absent-root branch (today's error, sink refusal intact). Chain-2 r2 (R1): a SHAVED corrective match of the stored root is REJECTED, never adopted — the stored identity and the pre-r1 miss policy are preserved (uuid_resolution_was_shave classifies the outcome; the speculative correction echo is surgically discarded; the raw root falls to the absent-root branch) — while an exact archived record still beats a shave upstream (E2) and keeps the archive repair. No second resolver and no per-carrier banner copy: the lens group atom's inherited root shares this exact seam via lens_engine._resolve_root.

occurrences.value: PUSH-TO-MODAL path for glimpse(push_to_modal=True): instead of RETURNING the rendered content to the agent, it COMMANDS the target Workflowy tab to render the requested SERVER-SIDE SCOPE into its docked Markdown modal -- the server-push twin of a human clicking APPLY. Chain-1 W4 (F5): the funnel's resolve-HERE-before-the-round-trip doctrine now covers the render_lens cell's atom roots too -- a root naming a visible archived node raises the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal (the docked modal never serves archives), so a push can never ack success and then fail tab-side. Chain-1 r2 (R2-W2): the resolve-HERE doctrine now covers every indirect selection as well -- a render_lens GROUP atom pre-flights its group's STORED root (an explicit root_handle override is the target and wins; a bare group atom rides the stored default, so a recursive merged lens cannot hide an archived effective root), the render_symbols cell resolves its roots and runs its items through the SHARED _resolve_lightning_rod_symbol_items_from_cache router (live legs first; an archived root or item refuses before any command; items still ride verbatim per D5), and the direct slice-group cell resolves the chosen group's STORED root when no override root is present. Handles the full (slice_group, root_uuid) truth table: slice_group only (resolve id-or-name -> canonical group_id via the SHARED Layer-1 _resolve_slice_group_handle -- the SAME id/prefix/case-insensitive-name resolver _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache uses), root_uuid only (resolve prefix-tolerantly via the SHARED resolve_uuid_like_node_handle -> a RAW-DUMP push, the zero-token 'show me this anchor' command), or BOTH (slice lens scoped to an override root). All resolution happens HERE (before the round-trip) so a bad group name / missing UUID fails loudly early. Sends a Direction-A 'apply_slice_in_dock' frame carrying whichever of {group_id, root_uuid} are present + the AGENT-SUPPLIED sort/since as an EXPLICIT override (never the tab's global dock sort) via the generic _ws_request_response rail; returns the tab's ack. The tab-side dispatch invokes the ONE shared applySliceGroupIntoDock (same fn the APPLY button uses), so the dock render + (for a slice) live-GUI-sync watcher are identical to a manual Apply; a raw-dump push installs NO watcher (no search/plan). The caller (glimpse) guards a bare live-DOM push (neither scope) as the only error.

occurrences.value: UUID-hallucination HARDENING for a render_spec-driven GLIMPSE (the render_spec="modal"/blob path). Given a deserialized RenderProjectionSpec + the /nodes-export cache map, canonicalize EVERY UUID the spec carries -- root_uuid, focus.uuid, and EVERY focus.ancestor_path entry -- through the SHARED prefix-tolerant Layer-1 resolver resolve_uuid_like_node_handle (the exact machine SCRY / anchor / snippet callers use). Grace runs BEFORE the exact (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) focus match downstream, so it only CANONICALIZES a possibly-drifted string to its cache UUID; it NEVER loosens the occurrence-exact match itself (a canonicalized triple still resolves to exactly one occurrence via _resolve_focus_index_path). On the render_spec="modal" path the UUIDs are already server-canonical (near-no-op belt-and-suspenders); on the pasted-blob fallback path this is the real net against an agent-drifted UUID in the chain. A UUID that stays unresolved (no exact hit, no unique prefix) or is ambiguous is LEFT AS-IS (best-effort): a bad focus already fails safe to the whole document downstream, and a bad root_uuid surfaces its own cache-miss error in the dispatch that follows. Returns a NEW spec via with_overrides; the input spec (frozen) is never mutated. Pure; no I/O beyond reading the passed cache map.

occurrences.value: The AGENT-OVERRIDE seam for the render_spec-driven GLIMPSE paths (render_spec="modal" AND the pasted-blob fallback). Given the RESOLVED, tab-sourced (or pasted) RenderProjectionSpec and the agent's TRI-STATE view overrides (as_markdown / headings_only / sort_by / sort_direction / since; None = inherit what the modal is showing, a value = explicit override), it (1) merges the non-None overrides onto the spec via the SINGLE normalized mutator spec.with_view_overrides (which re-runs the ONE normalizer and preserves the resolved kind via kind_hint -- NOT raw with_overrides), then (2) runs the LOUD combination guards ONCE on the FINAL merged spec, where spec.focus and spec.kind are known. The two guards (Dan-decided): (A) a sort override (sort_by/sort_direction supplied) is REJECTED when spec.focus is present -- sorting a single focused option-Y row is ill-defined; the user re-roots the modal at that subtree instead; (B) a since override is REJECTED when spec.focus is present (a tail/window over the whole underlying scope intersected with a focused row is meaningless). Beyond focus, the standard since preconditions are enforced by reading the FINAL SinceSpec object fields; curated requires a slice/slice_override scope. Returns (spec, None) on success or (spec, error_dict) on a rejected combination. occurrences.value: THE ONE agent-facing output-contract finalizer for the GLIMPSE FAMILY of MCP tools -- its consumers are the glimpse family (workflowy_glimpse), lightning_rod, anchor.dock.render, and slice_group render/sift/merge.render. Given the rich internal result dict every render helper builds, it delivers to the AGENT exactly what the human wants to see -- and nothing redundant. Rule: (1) output_file set -> pass the file-write summary through unchanged (the disk write is the deliverable, not the string). (2) result is not a dict -> already a bare value, pass through. (3) MARKDOWN / RAW-TEXT mode -- a RENDERED TEXT STRING is present -> return it RAW (real newlines, like read_text_file), NOTHING ELSE: preview_markdown (every Markdown-mode render across GLIMPSE live-DOM / slice_group / raw root_uuid / render_spec modal+blob / dom_capture, AND Lightning Rod render_tags/render_search/render_symbols) OR preview_text (the Lightning Rod gather raw-text tag outline, byte-identical to the modal's Gather). The rendered string IS the whole semantic payload in this mode, so no envelope is wanted. This is the single future-proof seam: ANY future raw-text mode just fills preview_text (or preview_markdown) and is delivered raw with ZERO further change here. (4) FULL / UUID mode -- a preview_tree is present -> return the STRUCTURED DICT, preserving preview_tree AND all the genuinely-useful metadata (node_count, depth, _source, render_scope, since_applied, ...), but STRIPPING ONLY the redundant CONTENT twins: `rows` (modal tree-view metadata that duplicates preview_tree) and any stray preview_markdown/preview_text; additionally, when headings_only=True (the compact UUID-harvest pass), strip bulky live-DOM raw `root`/`children` to keep the payload small. Full mode is for structural / UUID work, so the stats ARE wanted here -- only the duplicative rows/markdown clutter is dropped. (5) everything else (errors success:false, push_to_modal acks, gather's structured tag list when preview_text is somehow absent, empty payloads with neither field) -> pass the structured dict through unchanged so failures/acks still signal correctly. The rich internal payloads (rows, render_scope, since_applied, node_count) are LEFT INTACT on the helper returns -- they still flow to the browser/modal WS reply handlers that need them; this finalizer only shapes the AGENT-facing tool return. preview_markdown is checked before preview_text before preview_tree: at most one is ever populated on a given result, so order is belt-and-suspenders. STALE-FOCUS GUARD [ap:XDVDRG]: a Markdown/raw-text result that carries focus_unresolved is NEVER delivered raw -- its always-empty string would read as a legitimately empty view; the structured stale payload is returned instead (success flipped to false, the empty preview twins and modal rows dropped, error + focus_unresolved kept) so the shared family error boundary surfaces the loud stale-focus error. A legitimate empty (empty since-window, no focus_unresolved) still returns its raw '' when NO recency selection is active -- the (empty) stub then fires at the public funnel (9a); when a recency selection IS active ([ap:TVIIBN] 4e), the Markdown body is passed through the ONE empty-output stub (stub_empty_text_result, caveat C1) and the result opens with ONE '> Recency selection: ...' rule line naming what was chosen and teaching that sort_direction only orders (the structured full/UUID twin carries the same sentence as a top-level recency_header key, no quote marker). The header text is composed ONLY by _recency_header_sentence -- one composer, no second header writer; the browser modal / push / file paths never pass through here and are untouched by construction.

LIGHTNING ROD public MCP tool. Thin wrapper over the internal _lightning_rod_from_cache orchestrator: rate-limit acquire, then dispatch. Modes: gather (discover tags under a root -> feeds render_tags), render_tags (Option-B prefix-family tag filter; NO deprecation/suppress/expand semantics by DEFAULT -- the opt-in postfix_policy='slice' (ap:IMPPTX) instead routes it through the FULL Stage-1 funnel build_stage1_base_tree with the live postfix words + the real f8_global_never_expand_tags list), render_search (shlex 'smart' boolean/glob OR 'regex' free-text filter), render_symbols (dynamic tag-free beacon slice from a UUID/symbol/AP-ID list). Mutation modes: ensure_beacons/remove_beacon_tags (Q3 DISK beacons) and mutate_node_tags (Q4 batch Workflowy #tag add/remove/rename on NODES by UUID/[ap:CORE] handle -- operations-only; a thin ledger wrapper over the per-node tag primitives). Render modes are cache-only; no WebSocket (except one postfix config read for render_tags 'slice'), no slice-group persistence, no Workflowy-UI. Shared render knobs mirror glimpse and flow through render_stage2_filter_sort. since='curated' rejected (no slice tag set); live-GUI-sync never supported. The traversal pair rides the shared selection fragment ([ap:EPR86W] 4b): the walking verbs (gather/render_tags/render_search) carry recursive+descend_policy, and recursive=False is refused LOUDLY at the top of this body -- before the push branch, so a pushed selection cannot silently drop the request (one refusal text with the orchestrator's backstop, _lightning_recursive_refusal). The header names the selection/order, including 'N completed hidden' whenever the default completed-exclusion removed rows (recency views AND the plain inventory alike, U6/J11); under a recent-N selection [ap:TVIIBN] 4e adds ONE explicit rule line directly below the header (describe_dock_peek_recency_rule, the peek-side twin of the render verbs' _recency_header_sentence): sort_direction only orders the selected rows, it never changes which rows were chosen. Row handles ([ap:0M6VP8] peek half): rows without an AP-ID show a bracketed short UUID handle in the body by default; show_ids=true adds it to every row; both route through the ONE shortener unique_short_uuid_prefix over the caller's uuid_prefix_collisions index (CF-22/O3), never a second shortener. NEVER canonicalises to base_tags[0] (the old family-switch bug). families= names the family to write when the node carries more than one (dock_families_ambiguous otherwise; a family without a proper tag on the node is dock_family_not_on_node; --deprecated-only does not count as present). occurrences.value: ⚡ _anchor_point_promote_impl(items, handles, destination, tags, mode, children, include_completed, target_tab)

anchor.point.promote: the curation pass made atomic -- batch move-with-provenance (mode: move, default) and promote-as-COPY (mode: derivative). Two grammars (items=[{handle, destination, tags?, mode?, children?}] | handles=[...] + destination + tags? + mode? + children?) normalized by the pure normalize_promote_items before any I/O. Per item: resolve handle + destination through the generic resolver against ONE pinned cache map; origin = nearest ancestor Anchor Dock (global or local; else the immediate parent) via nearest_anchor_dock_ancestor; STRUCTURAL mapped-node refusal on source AND destination (_classify_node_map_state != 'unmapped' -- stricter than capture's guard, Markdown included) plus the first-line Cartographer-metadata content check (delegated to the ONE managed-metadata registry, managed_metadata.py). Batch grammar modelled on beacon.tags.ensure: per-item SKIP (unresolvable, not in cache, mapped) continues; batch REFUSE with zero writes (malformed, duplicate handles literal or same resolved UUID, destination inside the source's own subtree); STOP on any ambiguous post-send outcome (remaining rows not_run, nothing re-sent). MOVE = _node_move_impl(src, dest, 'bottom') + ONE _node_edit_core(note=trail+old, _tag_transform=add, _current_node=live) = 2 governed writes; the trail line '↩ moved from <origin> (<uuid8>) · <date>' is plain text, newest on top. MANAGED METADATA ([ap:BNNUZ4]): a note carrying a recognised managed block (program_interface YAML, estate payloads, manifests, snapshot/ledger names, … -- detect_trail_skip_metadata over the registry) STILL moves/copies but writes NO trail line: the move path skips the trail write (tags-only edit when tags are wanted, zero second writes otherwise; trail_written stays false) and the derivative path bakes no '↩ derived from' line; the row's info field names the kind and row["trail_line"] keeps the would-be line for provenance. DERIVATIVE = ONE subtree ETCH (_node_etch_sync_impl) built from the pinned cache with a fresh AP core reserved for the root and every AP-bearing descendant BEFORE the create (zero transient duplicate AP-IDs), decoded wire text, the '↩ derived from … · source [ap:X] <uuid8>' line baked into the root note and the tags into the root name; completed descendants skipped unless include_completed (then re-completed after the create via list_nodes + complete_node); children:false copies the root alone; the source is never written. ARCHIVED SOURCE (U2, Axiom 6/G8): a derivative's source may be an archived node -- the one sanctioned copy that reads archived content: move skips it with the §5.2.1 + how-to-copy story (reason archived_node, archive provenance on the row), derivative copies the archive file's VERBATIM records via ArchiveStore.verbatim_subtree_records (original names/parents/priorities, no 📦, no marker; text served verbatim, never re-decoded, E7), mints fresh AP-IDs, names the ARCHIVE as the trail-line origin ('↩ derived from archive "name" (basename, exported date) · date · source <uuid8>'), never installs an overlay, never touches the file; an archived DESTINATION refuses with §5.2.3 as a skipped row. Ledger in input order + summary; success only when every row landed; partial_success on mixed outcomes.

occurrences.value: Transport-free shared LensSpec projection core. Both the MCP family path and the docked-modal handler inject one already-read Lens Stage-0 snapshot, then reuse this single normalize/evaluate/materialize/sift implementation so canonical adoption, leaf algebra, and cache identity cannot drift. Threads the surface match_scope as the default for lens atoms that omit their own (recipe render = the surface value, default name-only; sift = 'name' for tag atoms while the query keeps its own name_and_note scope). A sift query returns sift_predicate -- the ONE build_search_predicate instance that decided the sifted tree -- so the MCP grep tier classifies its documents with the SAME predicate. The result ALWAYS carries lens_scaffold_ids ([ap:I506WY]): lens_engine.lens_scaffold_ancestor_ids receives the final tree, per-atom resolved roots AND the SAME pinned cache, so only strict input-root ancestors outside every member region become scaffold even when an input root is absent from the final tree. Every lens tail forwards this set to the existing materializer cause; ancestor_notes is folded producer-side. No second suppression path.

occurrences.value: THE single monotonic RENDER-GENERATION counter for the docked modal -- the keystone of the dock's async-render supersession model. A new render INTENT (a genuine selection change in setDockedSelection, a root-set/Refresh in prepareDockedServerRender, and -- as of the async dock-render-task refactor -- a slice APPLY/PUSH via displaySliceInDock) claims a fresh generation by ++dockedRenderGeneration; each async request captures the value it was fired under and acts ONLY if it still equals the current one at reply/paint time, so EVERY stale reply (success, failure, null, timeout) is dropped by ONE rule and a superseded render can never clobber a newer view. ONE shared clock governs BOTH the DOM-render path and the slice/push paint path (most-recent intent wins the paint chokepoint, independent of which async render finishes first). Historically unbeaconed, which hid it from the f8-expand/md-preview slice and led an architecture session to propose a NEW counter instead of extending this one; beaconed now so the next agent to touch async-render correctness sees it. NOTE: a bare top-level `let` is not symbol-addressable via read_text_snippet_by_symbol, so this block is also the read handle for the counter.

occurrences.value: Find-in-source query compiler for the dock Source view -- the HIGHLIGHT-only JS mini-twin of the server's build_search_predicate smart grammar (lightning_rod_search.py; twins-by-one-grammar, the SinceCodec-pair precedent). Tokenizes whitespace with "quoted phrase" support (unbalanced quote = loud {ok:false}), skips the OR/AND keywords and negated (- / !) terms (negation is meaningful for node FILTERING but not for highlight-in-place; ignored in v1), escapes every regex metacharacter then restores the * / ? GLOB wildcards, drops patterns that could match the empty string (a bare '*' would yield an infinite zero-length-match stream), and returns ONE combined case-insensitive alternation RegExp. occurrences.value: ƒ surfaceRenderFailure(res, opts): the single UI helper that turns a render/action reply into the right user-facing failure message

The ONE place that converts a dock render/action reply into a user-facing failure, so every caller surfaces the server's actionable text identically instead of a bare 'ERR' flash or a silent blank. Distinguishes the three failure modes the endpoint-liveness work defined: res==null -> TRANSPORT failure (no reply / cold socket / timeout); res.code=='unknown_endpoint' -> endpoint-liveness GHOST (tab dropped on an MV3 SW reconnect, already asked to re-register in the background -> retry), preferring the server's own res.error; res.success!==true -> any other structured failure surfaced verbatim (fallback to the caller's fallbackMessage). Returns true iff a failure was surfaced (caller early-returns), false on a success to render. UI propagation ONLY: shows a toast, optionally paints the message into the supplied dock render element and clears the source/leaf-count -- it NEVER renders content and touches no protocol/routing/retry/broker behavior.

Fire a Lightning Rod from the dock ribbon. mode is 'gather' | 'render_tags' | 'render_search'; the single text box feeds BOTH render modes (render_search verbatim as `query`, render_tags split on whitespace/commas into `tags`); matchScope ('name'|'name_and_note') rides inside the opaque lightning selection. Roots at resolveLightningRodRootUuid() (the current modal root; NO paste-a-UUID field). scoped (the 4th arg, ap:LRSCOPE/ap:LRHAND2) selects between TWO forks: (GLOBAL, scoped falsy) the original path -- build a kind='lightning_rod' RenderProjectionSpec and requestSliceModalRender -> displaySliceInDock, walking the WHOLE cache root; (SCOPED, scoped truthy) confine the search to the dock's CURRENT frozen artifact via requestScopedLightningDomCapture, producing an EPHEMERAL kind='dom_capture' result routed through displaySliceInDock -> the crack-closer -> displayScopedDomCaptureInDock (one-way door; the durable slice/raw origin is discarded, re-Apply to return). Scoped requires dockedFrozen; it sends the pinned captured tree (DOM-frozen) OR the durable base_render_spec + wasSlice (slice-frozen, server projects+filters), plus the optional occurrence-exact selected-row focus as the DOMAIN re-root pre-step (distinct from plain row-click navigation). occurrences.value: THE single client-side fan-out for a server-echoed render_scope (Option Y, Dan's 'server is the one choke point' model). Called by displaySliceInDock on EVERY successful cache-projected render, regardless of which SURFACE triggered it (a ribbon-widget click -> usually a no-op adopt of the client's own values; an MCP glimpse(push_to_modal=true) call -> a real update that lights up the ribbon). It (1) stores the whole scope in dockedRenderScope (footer display source), (2) mirrors scope IDENTITY into dockedSliceContext (the re-render/per-row scope handle: group_id + root_uuid), and (3) mirrors the VIEW params (sort_by/sort_direction/since/headings_only) into the per-tab render state via setTabModalState so the ribbon widgets + since field repaint to match. Adoption is fail-closed for invalid server-echo `since`: the scope is decoded before any state mutation, and a malformed/string wire value surfaces through the yellow bar and aborts adoption, preserving last-known-good state. Otherwise the since field's existing draft guard (refreshSinceHeadingsUi skips overwriting sinceInput while it is focused) is preserved so a reply landing mid-type never stomps the user's keystrokes. Pure UI/state fan-out; no I/O, no server round-trip.

occurrences.value: SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD (ap:LRSCOPE) EPHEMERAL display path — the destination of the crack-closer branch in displaySliceInDock for a kind='dom_capture' render_scope. It does NOT adoptRenderScope / normalizeRenderScopeToSpec / set dockedSliceContext.render_spec (that is exactly the launder the crack-closer prevents). Instead it RE-PINS the server-filtered forest as the dock's FROZEN-DOM-SINGLE captured tree (dockedRenderSource='dom', dockedFrozen=true, dockedFrozenSingleActive=true, dockedFrozenSingleTree/Rows set from meta.filtered_forest/rows), so EVERY downstream operation (per-row single render, sort/since via refreshFrozenDomAfterViewChange, frozenDomCapturedTree, resolveLightningRodRootUuid's DOM branch) is handled by the EXISTING frozen-DOM machinery with NO new per-consumer branching. This is the Lightning-within-Lightning wholesale forest replacement: the next Scoped run filters THIS pinned forest. Paints row 0's markdown immediately (raw_text for a gather outline, else marked); suppresses the scroll warning (complete by construction). Ephemeral by construction — nothing durable is stored, so it can never be Refreshed/re-projected as a cache scope.

occurrences.value: Centralized capture of the `since` validation/empty-window signal from ANY docked-modal render reply (DOM or slice; snapshot, single, apply, refresh). On a since_error refusal (success:false + since_error) it stashes the human error string into dockedServerSinceError so applyDockedServerWarning paints the yellow bar at TOP priority (the render was refused -- supersedes the staleness/root bars); otherwise it clears the error and records empty_window (a VALID empty result -> an informational note, not an error). Also repaints the fine-print footer. Returns true iff a since_error was captured so callers can early-out (avoid the local-render fallback that would show stale content instead of teaching the invalid combination).

occurrences.value: KaTeX math rendering for the docked Markdown modal (Dan, 2026): self-registering bootstrap that installs a SMALL CUSTOM marked extension (defined in THIS file -- the vendored stock marked-katex-extension was tried first, then REPLACED after a live false-positive report) onto the global marked instance at content-script load, so inline $...$ and display $$...$$ in composer strings render as math at the ONE existing choke point (composedMarkdownToHtml -> marked.parse) with ZERO call-site / server / spec / wire changes. GRAMMAR (pandoc-flavored, v2): opening $ must NOT be followed by whitespace; the content may NOT contain '$' or a newline; the content may NOT end in whitespace; the closing $ must NOT be followed by a digit (the currency guard: 'costs $5 and $10' stays plain text). The '$'-free content rule makes the reported failure IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION: the stock grammar REJECTED legitimate math immediately followed by ')' (its trailing lookahead admitted only [ws ?!.,:] or end, so '$0.50$)' failed), and because stock content COULD span a '$', the orphaned '$' then ran away to a distant later '$' and rendered a whole prose paragraph as red broken TeX. A match here can never cross a '$', so a misfire is bounded to one short span, never a paragraph. Also fixed vs stock: math immediately followed by ')' ';' ']' etc. now RENDERS, including parenthesized math like '($p < 0.05$)' (the stock start() required the opening '$' at start-or-after-space and missed that too). Broken TeX still degrades to red source (throwOnError:false) with a try/catch escaped-raw fallback. Block display math is '$$' on its own lines ('$$\n...\n$$', multi-line content allowed); a single-line '$$x$$' renders as inline displayMode. Load order is pinned in manifest.json: marked.min.js -> katex/katex.min.js -> THIS file -> glimpse-cache-client.js; KaTeX css + fonts are injected via the manifest (katex/katex.min.css + katex-overrides.css; fonts via web_accessible_resources). No-ops with a console.warn if marked/katex are absent, so a vendoring slip degrades to the old plain render, never a broken dock.
